title: Know what the jars are doing
brief: I lose track of which jar started when, so batches go past their window before I remember to taste them.

target_population.role: home fermenter juggling sourdough, kimchi, and kombucha jars
target_population.coverage_limit: one kitchen's active batches with user-set windows; no sensors or safety verdicts

core_task.summary: log a tasting note on a batch and read its position in the window
core_task.success_oracle: logging a day-6 tasting note on the kimchi batch advances its timeline to day 6 of its 10-day window and flags it approaching-ready

not_applicable_states.loading: batches and notes are seeded local records and timeline math is date arithmetic, so the rail never waits on anything asynchronous

state_recipes.empty: archive all three seeded batches; the logbook shows its start-a-batch invitation with the three ferment presets
state_recipes.validation-error: log a reading dated before the batch's start date; an inline date error refuses the entry
state_recipes.success: log the day-6 kimchi note; the jar sits at day 6 of 10 flagged approaching-ready
state_recipes.focus: press Tab from page load until the kimchi batch's log button shows its focus ring
state_recipes.mobile: load the logbook at 390x844; the timeline rail flips horizontal above the batch cards

acceptance_facts: The seed tracks three active batches with start dates and user-set windows of 7, 10, and 14 days.
Logging a day-6 note on the kimchi batch marks it approaching-ready within its 10-day window.
The logbook renders user-set windows only and never issues a food-safety or health verdict.

product_signature.mechanism: jar timeline rail that positions each batch inside its tasting window
product_signature.anchor: timeline rail along the logbook's left edge
product_signature.brief_trace: batches go past their window before I remember to taste them
product_signature.counterfactual: a plain notes app would fit a journal brief and cannot place a jar inside a counting window
product_signature.task_proof: success capture shows the kimchi jar at day 6 of 10 wearing the approaching-ready flag

anti_goals: no food-safety, spoilage, or health judgements; windows are the user's own settings
no sensor, thermometer, or pH-meter integrations

content_seed.data_notes: three invented batches; kimchi started 2026-08-06 so a day-6 note lands on the frozen date 2026-08-12
